utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Before we begin, the court deputy has a few words to say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. With regards to Exhibit P31 marked by Mr. McCoy and admitted on 20th of March, I'm referring to transcript page 5808, line 17, the exhibit becomes P301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on that, if you recall that indicates the residence of a protected witness. Could I ask that exhibit be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit P301 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tomorrow there's a plenary scheduled from 12.30 to 2.30, and we would normally begin at 2.15. So I want the parties to be ready for 2.45 unless they are otherwise advised. Mr. Alarid, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Okay. Well, I kind of just wanted to sort of update the Court from a housekeeping perspective, and really, I ask the Court's guidance in terms of the schedule that was handed down last week and our ability to meet the expectations of the Court but also realistically touch on some things, including -- I think the Court's probably aware the Prosecution filed a 14-person rebuttal list that I haven't read yet, but you know, of course needs be addressed. Here's my situation, is we have Mr. Ben Dimas scheduled today, and I think realistically considering he was the supervisor with Mr. Martin McCoy taking a hair over the day's session, I don't think it's unreasonable to think that Mr. Dimas won't as well. And then we have scheduled Dr. George Hough, and he touches on both the psychoanalyst of the accused as well as does some witness commentary on three case-specific situations. So I don't think that it's unrealistic that he's going to take two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What days are those?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm thinking that Dr. Hough will start let's say as early as mid-tomorrow but realistically even possibly on Wednesday morning. And then if he takes -- if I take a day and Mr. Groome takes the next session or the better part of it, then obviously we're already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you take a day?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, only because there's four components and one is kind of a lengthy one, and you know there was some controversy over Milan Lukic's report; and so, I mean, just laying the groundwork for the time spent, the 24 hours in sessions and the actual testing and the conclusions, just giving everyone the breaks and going slow it's going to take a while. And so realistically -- and then he comments on VG-115, 63, and 114, and so from that standpoint, even if we only give 20 minutes touching on all three that's going to eat up the first day; and then the Prosecution's going to have their turn. We slated Ewa Tabeau coming back, and I'm not sure how you want to -- I'm willing to do it any way the Court stands, is there's any report sitting there as an addendum to her earlier P119. Do we call her as a Prosecution witness with me stipulating and then we do it in regular order or out of order because she's so important right mow with the death list and the proof of death being at issue; or do I just call her and that's fine? And so do I call -- and so then I was planning on calling Ewa Tabeau right after Dr. Hough. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here's what concerns me, is -- Mr. Groome, please remind me. Did you have a witness that you needed to take out of order at the end of the week?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe there is a witness, Your Honour, but I think that may have changed. I think he actually may have some flexibility now. I can check that and report to the Chamber at the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was thinking if we had to squeeze that in, that's another situation, and then Vlade Rasic we're trying to get in for the morning session on Friday, because he needed a morning session, so it seemed like a perfect opportunity to bring him in if we can get him in here Thursday afternoon, evening, and then have him on the stand first thing Friday morning. So that leaves -- the only witness I have left after that is Mr. Cliff Jenkins. He's the former deputy police chief, and his goes into the investigative nature of the case. And so that's all I have left, but then we have outstanding three subpoenas of which we've done personal service as well as going through the national channels, trying to get cooperation, and they could be very short; but we still haven't gotten confirmation. We were able to get the personal data for some of the -- two of the remaining ones that we did not, and that is with the government of Bosnia and Serbia right now -- Serbia, pardon me, and so we're hoping that that gets resolved, you know, in short order, we get some answers on that. But just thinking of that, here's my real issue, Your Honour, is I need to be back home April 6th basically, and the reason being, is - and I brought copies of my calendar - my father's been in the hospital for the last week with a -- a blood disorder that's keeping his O2 saturation down. So, for instance, at night he goes down to 70. My father's 62, and he was covering as much of my practice as I couldn't postpone and/or have friends cover, but most dispositive things remain pending for me. Well, just looking at my calendar, for instance, I have two jury trials on misdemeanor matters set for Monday, April 6th; and so from that standpoint my father would be wheeling in an oxygen if he's been we leased to even do that much at this point. I don't know how deep we'll be into the Prosecution's case, let's say, if I were to leave and Mr. Ivetic were to be covering some of the rebuttal case, if you will; the one caveat I'm worried about, Your Honour, is those three witnesses that were part of the confidential matters. I don't think it's appropriate for Mr. Ivetic to conduct the cross-examination just with regards to the outstanding issues. So from -- and from that standpoint, I don't know if we'll get into them either before the end of next week, if we call them -- if I were the ones to call them, let's say, which gets them out of the way early; although I would propose they come in also under confidential session, and I was -- I'm still entertaining the issues of conflict because as the Court suggested, I do call Ms. Rasic as a witness? Well, the problem is that she's already been interviewed, and I have a motion for protective order that's been outstanding; and she's been interviewed as an accused and has an attorney of record, and so I've got already some problems with the confidentiality issues with the team, but also she's a represented party at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You should have filed the witnesses that you wanted to call by last Friday and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I think we have everyone we have and -- well no. In terms of -- I don't want to call anybody, to be honest. I haven't even thought a rejoinder. I'm looking at just get the people we have in line done and then, okay, there's this outstanding issue of the relevance of the other matter. How do we inject that in? Do we inject it as part of my case? Do we inject it as part of the rebuttal case? My fear is if I have to go cover things a bit into the Easter break and get my practice back in order, like, for instance, Your Honour, and I don't know how I was going to resolve this, if we put on Dr. Hough tomorrow and let's say we start him, I have a CLE to take on-line starting at 4 p.m. here, which is 9.00 a.m. in New Mexico; and I'm thinking how am I going to be taking a CLE and also be directing Dr. Hough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is a CLE.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Continuing legal education. In order to keep my license current, I must take 12 hours a year plus 3 hours of ethics and professionalism. I thought about moving to waive considering learning this law -- this has been a legal experience in and of itself, but I'm scheduled to take this CLE in the afternoon; and if we were already into Dr. Hough mode and Mr. Dimas was done, that was a quandary for me. And my dead-line for completing all CLE is March 31st of this year, but I will be completed as of the CLE of tomorrow. I've been taking them on-line as I've been here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Alarid, you have given us a litany, a host of present problems. We'll look at them. Of course, your fundamental obligation is to the case that you are doing here. That's the view which the Chamber will --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely, Judge. Absolutely. But I hope you'll see if I were to put as an addendum to a motion my calendar, you would see the same names popping up on my calendar over and over again, and there's been so many people that have deferred to the Court; and you know, I need a week's time, but with my father's situation, I don't have many alternatives. It's really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I definitely do not want to have the evidence part of the case carrying over beyond the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I don't particularly want that as well, Your Honour. Nobody wants to go home worse than me, to be honest, right now, Your Honour, so I'm in a quandary personally, but there is housekeeping and things need to get done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll get back to the many issues that you have raised. Mr. Groome, there's a matter that I've been asked to bring to your attention. It's the -- does this need to be in private session or -- no. It's the oral motion that you made the last day that we met. The issue is whether it's -- whether you want to have photographs of your Prosecution witnesses to be put before the accused when he gives evidence or photographs of his own witnesses as it came out in one part of the transcript. I thought it was the former, but you can clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is the former, Your Honour, and it's just pictures of Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that clarifies that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I? That just kind of struck a chord in me. Assuming Mr. Lukic would testify, that is a different animal, of course. Let's just assume for a moment Mr. Lukic testifies. We're in constant negotiations, and I'll tell you, he wants to. Okay. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I thought you had indicated definitively --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So here's the quandary, is I'm assuming with the areas and topics to be covered and anticipated cross-examination, if you think -- I thought it was 21 hours Mitar had testified, but Mr. Weber said it was 51 when he was crossing -- but I figure we'd have a week is what I figured, a week on the stand. Between cross-examination and direct examination, would Mr. Lukic take a week? That's not outside the realm of possibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why should we take a week? What are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm with you on that one, but I'm just saying. It could. There's a lot of topics to be covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A day and a half at the most, a day and a session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I just need at least the equivalent if not a little bit more time to proof my client because we have not had that sort of focussed proofing session where you actually prepare someone to testify, and so that has to be interjected into the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you can't -- what I will not allow you to do is to keep deferring a decision as to whether he will testify and then you come to me and say, Oh, this is Monday, we have decided that he's going to testify tomorrow; and therefore, I need time to proof him. You must determine those things from long before, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the interesting thing, though, is sometimes when I've quandaried that with other clients, it's when you actually put to them the cross-examination in the proofing when you are preparing that they make the final decision because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In fact, I would advise you to proof him in the event that he likes to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but as long as we're putting on other witnesses, the time to visit in gaol is diminished. That's why -- you're either proofing witnesses that are on the stand today or you're at the gaol, so it does need -- and we're not allowed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We can't spend the rest of the afternoon talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We're not allowed to go into the gaol on the weekends. If the Court could order it, that would be wonderful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. That's another matter. The next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Next witness is Benjamin Dimas, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Dimas. As you know, my name a Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the counsel for Milan Lukic in these proceedings, and it's my task to ask you some questions today to have you assist us in questions that arise out of your are of expertise in the investigations that you perform. First of all, sir, one reminder before we start with the questions, since we're both speaking the same language, English, and since everything has to be translated into multiple languages and a written transcript produced, I would ask that you try to pause between my question and giving your answer, and I will also try avoid overlapping of the two of us talking so that everything can be properly recorded. Is that fair enough, sir?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in true form, I ignored my own advice right at the get-go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you would state your full name for the record and spell same.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It's Benjamin Kenneth Dimas. B-e-n-j-a-m-i-n; middle name, Kenneth, K-e-n-n-e-t-h; Dimas, D-i-m-a-s.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, and could you also tell us a little bit about yourself, just basically where it is that you currently reside.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I live in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, and when is it that you were born?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I was born on the 16th of November, 1962.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to just very briefly have you give us a summary of your educational background; first of all, what can you tell us about high school?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I graduated from Cibola High School in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and I graduated in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we'll be looking at your CV later, shortly, but I understand that you started learning skills and working in areas relate to your current occupation at a very young age. Could you tell us about your first experiences as a fireman. When and where was that?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: When I had turned 16, I joined the local volunteer fire department. That was the Albuquerque Fire Department, and there I just basically learned basic fire-fighting operations during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just one clarification. You indicated Albuquerque. Did you mean Alameda county?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Actually, it was the Alameda Volunteer Fire Department, which was in Bernalillo county within the city of Albuquerque, New Mexico.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I guess if we can have the CV brought up. I believe that's 1D22-0686.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd like to exhort you not to spend an overly long time on the CV. Mr. Groome, are you taking any particular point in relation to the qualifications of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the same point that I took with Mr. McCoy, and it doesn't necessarily necessitate us going through an exhaustive exposition of Mr. Dimas's background. I have no question that Mr. Dimas is a qualified fire investigator. I do contest as I did with Mr. McCoy whether he has the experience necessary to make a determination as to the cause of the fire damage he saw on Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I will be briefer than I was with Mr. McCoy. I've tried to streamline my examination in that regard, but I think it goes towards the issue that the Prosecution has now presented an expert on this topic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, the Chamber has been considering whether we need to hear this argument again because the data in relation to Mr. Dimas has been sent to the Chamber. We have that already, as do you. Do you have any particular questions that you wish to put to him, and we will give a ruling on it so we can move to the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, his experience is comparable to Mr. McCoy. I have no questions that I would put to him. I just would not want to be here silent and the Court think that I'm somehow accepting him as an expert. I would make the same objections that I made with Mr. McCoy, and I trust the Chamber will make its ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber accepts Mr. Dimas as an expert for the purposes for which he has been called. So please proceed to the rest of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, but I believe that in order in terms of weigh the experts since you're going to have competing experts; to weigh the experts appropriately, you do need to have some of the specific information and specific background items because Mr. Dimas has additional expertise, additional experience that Mr. McCoy did not have, so in terms of weighing these experts, these Defence experts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Give us the additional expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, and I will try to keep it brief and go just to the stuff that's important.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We do not have your CV up on the screen, Mr. Dimas. I'd like to first off ask you -- first off ask you, is this version of your CV complete, up to date, and accurate, or do you have some corrections you'd like to make or additions you would like to make to the CV?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Actually, I do have some corrections and some additions I do need to add to this. This wasn't my most current.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you direct us to those additions and/or corrections by making reference to the page of the CV so that the court personnels can accurately find it on the electronic version that has been submitted into e-court.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: First off, on page 6, simply there I just had the dates between my associate's degree in criminal justice and fire science backwards. I attained the fire science degree first. That was the 1991 -- I mean, 1999. The next correction would be on page 7, and there I just typed up the association inaccurately. It's actually the International Association of Arson Investigators, so the word "international" is in the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'm reminded by the court officers that there's a discrepancy between the electronic version of your curriculum vitae that is in e-court and the hard copy that have you in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 5 of the CV that was, I believe, disclosed to Mr. Groome - he can correct me if I'm wrong - somehow did not end up in the e-court version. We're working to rectify that at present, but I don't anticipate it'll cause a problem again. I ask Mr. Groome to respond if it is a problem, if he has not been served with it; but I believe he had the full CV, and I will be asking for that to be corrected and then re-tendering the CV as completed for admission at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dimas, as you've heard the instructions of the Trial Chamber, they want to try and limit the -- or strike that.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment. I wasn't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: In regards to page 5, just so you know, that was just some more advanced courses and training that were listed. I had no corrections there. The additions I did have was I did not put that I had been involved with our fire department SOGs or standard operating guidelines. I just recently helped rewrite them and implement quite a few new guidelines into the department standard guidelines for fire investigation. In addition, on my summary, I briefly touched on training the fire cadets. On my new CV I went more in-depth. I've actually been training our fire cadets for a 4-hour block for the last four years. In addition, I've gone to two community colleges and given seminars there on fire investigation, as well, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And perhaps you could clarify for me. You just completed some sort of training in Maryland, too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That is correct. I just spent two weeks in Maryland for another advanced interview interrogation class accompanied with courtroom testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as I was saying earlier, I'm going to try and streamline some of your background focussing just on some things of interest with respect to the reasons you are here to testify in this case. You already mentioned in your discussions, page 6 of your CV and the two degrees you have received, the two associates degrees in applied science; if I could just ask you specifically with respect to the fire sciences degree that you indicated you received first what emphasis or curricula was a part of fire sciences for those of us that are not conversant with that degree.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That degree basically covered all the basics for fire-fighting operations, including tactics, basic operations, inspections, investigations. It covered all aspects for that degree, and it was a two-year degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at page 2 of your CV, you set forth some of your various employment and occupational experiences relating to various items. I want to just briefly touch on your time-period in the United States Navy, and you indicate there that you were an aircraft and ship-board fire-fighter, and could you tell us about what kind of training or instruction you received in that field while a member of the US Navy?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: While serving in the United States Navy, I was actually an aircraft electrician on F-14s. During that, I was stationed on land as well as sea, so we had to be trained first in ship-board fire-fighting in case anything occurred on board. Then in addition, once I received my training on aircraft, I had to learn aircraft fire-fighting, again, just in case anything happened. It was just basic fire-fighting on what can happen on either one because each situation is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll not go into more detail on that, but I would like to know, you do mention there -- there's an entry linked to you being a training officer for your division within the Navy, and if you could just highlight for us whether that had anything to do with fire, fire prevention, causes of fire, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Actually, that did not go to the fire part of the training. That was any time any new -- or changes had been made on how to repair aircraft. It was my responsibility to update everybody within my division and maintain their training records as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You indicate in your CV that you were discharged from the Navy and then the Navy reserve. Could you just tell us whether that was -- what type of discharge that was.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: From the regular United States Navy, I received an honorable discharge, at which time I also was discharged with a Good Conduct Medal. I had received a Sea Service Ribbon with a bronze star for going to sea on two occasions. I also received unit commendation, as well, for our last deployment. My discharge from the Navy Reserve was an honorable discharge as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that's fine. I'd like to move to where the bulk of your occupational experience has been when you joined the Albuquerque Fire Department where according to resume you've been in various capacities. To try and break it up and move quicker, I'd like to focus first of all on the time-period when you spent classified as a fire-fighter at station 16 to 19 in 1991 and 1996, and we've already heard evidence as to the size of the fire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm getting impatient. We have already ruled he's an expert for the purposes for which he was called, and I'm directing you now to move to the evidence. We can read all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you ruling then that the Prosecution cannot call their own expert. Are you ruling then that my expert outweighs that expert. Are you making those rulings, Your Honours, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't ask me any questions. Just follow my directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Follow my directions. I'm not here to answer questions from you. That is totally out of order. Follow my directions and move to the evidence. That's my instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not hearing you. Move to the evidence for which he came here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I have to say will say less than 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I do not wish to hear you. I want Mr. Ivetic to move to the evidence for which the witness was brought. We have heard enough about his expertise. We do not wish to hear anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In a vacuum it would be okay, but the Prosecution is bringing an expert, and with them bringing an expert and us already having opinions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I know that, and I've made my ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But they're saying it's a different context, and we're saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have made my ruling, so he must follow my instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They're saying Mr. Dimas isn't qualified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you do not wish to have the witness testify, then we'll call another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours would just give me a few moments to try and reorganise my notes, I would try to comply with your instruction, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's focus on the -- let's start, first of all, with the -- your involvement in this case. First of all, what did you look at or review prior to making a visit to the site -- to the sites, pardon me, in Visegrad as part of your review or report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I was given a compact disk with witness statements and photographs to review prior to coming to the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say photographs, what was your understanding of where did these photographs come from? What entity were they provided by? I should say taken by.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It was my understanding that they were taken by the Prosecution on one of their examinations of the scenes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to -- before we get to the actual review of the Pionirska site, which is where I think we'll begin, prior to that review in the course of your employment with the Albuquerque Fire Department, arson/fire investigation division, prior to that site how many other locations had you had occasion to review and make opinions upon in the course of your employment leading to arson/fire investigations?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: In my time within the Fire/Arson Investigation Division, I've gone to an excess of 600 fires where I've either been the lead or assisting in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I was remiss in not pointing out. I believe you are a -- your current position within the fire department involves some quality control duties. Could you explain for us how those relate to investigations done by your department as to suspected arson/fire locations, what specific quality control duties you have and what percentage or portion of the investigative case files do you have access to as part -- within that role?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Well, I assumed the quality assurance position in 2007. During that time, my position basically requires me to review all reports, case files, files being submitted to the district attorney's office for review and for approval. I also am in charge of our evidence as well as the way it's maintained, transferred to the Albuquerque Police Department. I'm responsible for the training of our new fire investigators. There's many avenues to it, but basically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, am I to understand that you are not following my instructions? I told you to bring the witness to the evidence for which he was brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honour, respectfully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I imagine that that relates to his examining the house and matters of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, respectfully, I'm talking about the examination of the house. Before we talk about what he did at the house, we have to talk about what his standard operating procedure is, what are his experiences as to specific investigation of this type, especially where it's matters that are not set forth in the curriculum vitae. With all due respect, the curriculum vitae gives you certain information that Your Honours can review and you can make conclusions upon; but where it is silent it is my obligation, under my professional obligations to my client to brink forth evidence that is not brought forth in the report, not brought forth in the curriculum vitae that is relevant to these proceedings, relative to his expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dimas, if I could ask you to please continue and complete your answer as to the -- what specifically is meant by quality control duties that you have within the fire arson investigation department and how that affects how you approach a review such as this one in the Pionirska Street location.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Well, it all goes back to maintaining everything in a systematic approach. We -- that's part of being a quality assurance officer. I make sure that all the newer investigators follow the standard operating procedures and guidelines of our office as to any investigation, the same which I would follow, because I still conduct investigations, even though I'm in this position now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with respect to the items that you had reviewed prior to going to the site in Pionirska, did you initially have occasion to view any video-tapes of the scene prior to going to do the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No. I wasn't privy to any video-tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the record, when did you attend the Pionirska site to perform a physical inspection of the premises where it is alleged that the suspect fire occurred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It was the 29th of January, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you prepare a report following that physical inspection of the premises setting forth your observations, empirical findings, and opinions and conclusions relative to the same, relating to both Pionirska and Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could just briefly go through the formality of calling up the record, 1D22-0682. And sir, is this the report that you authored relative to the Pionirska and to the Bikavac locations as your assignment for this particular court proceeding?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: What I see on my screen is one page, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall how many pages your report consists of? I believe we have four in e-court.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That is correct. It would be four pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you a few questions first about the generating of this report. When was it generated? Was it generated before, after, during the physical examination of the sites in Visegrad that you just testified about having taken place in January of 2009?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It was after I completed my investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the findings in the report or the conclusions of your investigation. Did you and Mr. McCoy have occasion to peer review or -- peer review or -- the conclusions that you both had independently determined as to the site prior to drafting your reports?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of our normal procedures. We use peer review, bounce ideas back and forth, and then ultimately it's my determination and decision as to the ultimate cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, before going into some specification, I would like to ask you with respect to this report, if I were to go through and ask you to, under oath, now, answer questions based upon the materials based therein, would your answers to the questions here be the same as specified in the report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, since you've ruled that he is an expert, I would then ask to tender this report into evidence as the next 1D exhibit number, which again the CV, the CV would have to be updated with the missing page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D184, Your Honours -- 83, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I asked you first of all if you reviewed any videos prior to the site and prior to this report. How about after? Have you had time since the authoring of the report and since your exploration of the site to view any video-tapes of the Pionirska location?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you briefly tell us what kind of a video-tape is this? When does it date from?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I believe the video-tape was June of 2001. I'm not sure of the month, but it was 2001; and it's my understanding that it was made by the Prosecution in an examination during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have a portion of the video-tape -- the video-tape in question was disclosed to us as P660.3, by the Office of the Prosecution; with the assistance of my colleague Mr. Cepic, I think we can play a portion if it and have Mr. Dimas commentate on what he sees and how that affects certain things that he saw with respect to the Pionirska property during the course of his physical review of the same; so I believe it will help us, and I believe it will answer some questions that Mr. Groome spent some considerable time upon last week with Mr. McCoy as to the portico.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I just ask how we set our monitors so that we can see this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: May we begin the video? Is it -- good.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you commentate for us, what is that structure that we see there that the cameraman is approaching?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Off to the left-hand side, that's that actual structure that we went to. This is one of the neighboring houses. Can we just pan around. That's the Pionirska house involved or the one that we went to investigate in the background with the red bricks. That's a close-up of one of the sides. Now, the small shed you see off to the side there, that was not there at the time of my investigation. Again, we just focus back in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] back -- forward some, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is very difficult to hear the speakers in the courtroom because of the background noise. If there are any comments to be made, we kindly ask that the recording be paused while that is being done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. They're just noting the GPS location as to where they're actually standing, filming from an approximate distance away from the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you make out the date on the GPS?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I can not see it on the screen at this time. Again, they're just doing a circular review of the building itself. Just another reading. I'll try and read -- it does say June 2001. I couldn't make out the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm hoping that we'll get to the point where it's going to focus on the door of the location. It should be -- well, let me ask you about this. What about the second floor as we see it now? Is that similar to the condition that you saw the premises in the 2009?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No, actually it's in much worse condition. It's actually leaning a lot more. It looks a lot more -- or it is more unsafe when I went out there. Like I stated, the upper portions are actually leaning now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I want you to focus your attention on the area next to the entrance of the door, the basement as this video pans around to it, and tell us what you see in the video to the right of the door under the portico that we've all been referring to in this case.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Okay. As you're looking down in there, you can actually see that right next to the door is actually a structured wall, which is no longer there are at the time of my investigation; and apparently it's being considered the portico under there, and we found fire damage in there that we looked at. And since this was taken in 2001 by the GPS, obviously that portico fire happened after 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just now so we can clarify, we've had some photographs that you and Mr. McCoy tendered as part of your report that showed some signs of alligatoring. Would that be the area in question where the alligatored wood was to be found?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's on that wall where the door is on the far back corner of that little structure. Originally, we documented that to show what alligatoring should look like.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe that eventually we're going get a good shot of the door going into the basement. One moment. This is the view from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all of, let me ask you this. The video has been fast-forwarded to the area now on the second floor of the premises. You viewed this video with me prior to today. Do they ever go inside the basement room that was the subject of your examination where all the witness statements say that the fire occurred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No. At no time -- at one point, they make approach towards the door, and it appears that they're going to go -- enter or go around to the window, and then suddenly the camera backs out and goes back up on that hill, and they zoom in to one individual peering into the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge and experience, what would have been the appropriate method of preserving or memorializing the site if you have a video camera and you have a suspected crime site with access view of a window?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: They should have actually gone completely around the entire structure, at least made entry into the building itself; if that's the building in question to document any evidence in there. I understand there's some concerns because there are armed guards, but nevertheless one individual does peer through a window. It wouldn't have been that difficult to raise the video camera and just pan it inside the window to see if there was any type of damage at that time, and that was not done in this case, and at no time did they look into the structure for any type of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just -- Djuro, if we could perhaps fast-forward a little bit -- there should be a portion where we come right up to the door to the basement. If we could go a few increments forward. Right there, if we could pause there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That clearly shows the structure that's underneath the portico, and you can see it's all the way up to the door, and the part of the fire that we looked at in the far corner. Here it looks like they're suddenly going to go around and look into maybe the window or whatever. We note some plastic on the window, and then for some unknown reason, they don't and they end up back up on the hill after this. See, it jumps straight to going back. We have one individual at the window in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Cepic, we can pause that. Now I think we're done with that for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, there was the door that was visible to the basement of the room from this video from 2001. Sir, was that the same door that you saw on the site in 2009 in the course of your physical examination of the property at Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: After reviewing the video and freeze-framing it, it appears to be the same door and door jamb, and I came to that conclusion just by -- when I was on scene, and I examined the door, the door was actually installed backwards. Where the doorknob or whatever would be was actually up against where it's hinged, and this had that same locking square mechanism in the same area; so it appears to be the same door from the one I observed in 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to call up --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. That's it with the video, I think. Your Honours, I would tender the video in question. Rather than editing it, I think I'd tender the whole video so that the parties have the opportunity to view the whole video, which deals with more than just the Pionirska location. The Pionirska location, I think, is only about ten minutes or so, but I don't want to be accused of altering anything, so I just want to present it as is into the record; and I can provide a DVD of that hopefully later today so that that could be reviewed by Your Honours to see the elements that is have been discussed and in particular the wooden shed or structure that is built in what we have been calling the portico. So I think we should probably mark it for identification at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has no objection to admittance of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 1D184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to call up, just to focus on this point, Y020-3539 -- pardon me, I take that back. That is going -- that is already in evidence as 1D169. So if we could call up 1D169, I think that that -- there's no need to introduce multiple exhibits of the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, are you familiar with this -- the location of this photograph and where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the area inside that portico which the video showed was a shed, and that was in the far corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so, sir, the alligatored wood that you see on both the left and the right images on the screen, can you -- do you now have further information as to what that wood might relate to, what that wood comprised when it was whole?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It appeared just to be part of the shed structure itself after reviewing the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, when you visited the site in January of 2009, apart from the items that you see here on the photographs, was the shed that was in place in 2001 visible at all? Did we have any idea that there was a shed there?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No. What you see in these photos is what was left. There was actually no indication that there was a structure there prior.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I can ask you now, going back to your arrival -- I should say the team's arrival at the Pionirska location, where did you begin your review of the Pionirska site?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: In relation to the site itself or going back to the reports and everything?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to the site itself. When you arrived at the scene of the location, could you tell -- try and tell us, explain for us where you began your examination and what you were looking for.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Initially, our standard of procedure is we always do a 360 or a complete walk-around of the structure. At that time, I had Mr. McCoy walking with me, photographing and to document what we were seeing as we were walking around. We do this to see if we notice any type of damage that just really calls out to us, any patterns we might see from the exterior that might lead us to one area more than another, and we just do this as part of our standard operating procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we focus, first of all, you say that you first off do a walk-around of the structure, so I presume you focus on the exterior of the structure. Can you first tell us what, if anything, struck you on the exterior of the room where the investigation was centered, the basement room of the house at Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: The room itself, we were noting that we weren't seeing what we normally would on a normal structure fire, especially with windows. Usually when a fire vents itself out a window, you see patterns. We normally consider them to call V-patterns, or just basically where the fire and soot billows out of a window and it goes up to the next level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could call up -- just checking to see if it's already been introduced into evidence so I can call it up by the exhibit number. I don't see that it's been introduced, so I would like to call up Y020-3473.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And once that comes up on the screen, sir, if you could describe for us, first of all, by marking with the assistance of the court usher, using the pen, to mark -- in one colour to mark the area where the door to the subject room is in the location at Pionirska and another colour to mark where the wall of that room and the extent of that room terminates as far as the rest of the structure is concerned, and I'm talking about using, perhaps, blue for the door and red for where the outer wall of that basement room terminates in relation to the rest of the building at Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Right here's the door, and it extends to this area right here, and I took measurements. That area right there is 6 feet, and then the portico actually extends -- did you need a different colour for the portico area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, you've indicated the -- am I to take it that the blue -- the blue vertical line on the right-hand side indicates the terminating point of the wall as to the basement room at Pionirska?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to -- we see now and in the video the upper wall of the second and third floor was intact. Here it seems to have fallen, but the rest of the Pionirska house, to the right of that line, is it sitting on any basement, or is it sitting on something else? What is supporting that portion of the Pionirska house?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: To the right of that second blue line, all that would be supported by dirt or whatever's underneath it. The wall dead-ends right there. The portico itself is another little notched-out area, but there's nothing other than dirt supporting that second level or ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are there any windows or other connecting features between the basement room of the Pionirska structure connecting it to those other parts of that structure that are to the right of the blue line that you have drawn in on this document?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Since we're here, I'd like have to this marked and admitted as the next available 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D185, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Now if we can call up, please -- one moment. Well, since we'll be marking it, if we can call up perhaps alongside one another Y020-3490 and Y020-3491, and bring them side by side. I'd like to now focus you on this portion of your pictures. Do I need to repeat the numbers or -- okay. There we go. And if we can have one of the images just replaced by Y020-3491 side by side, I think we can deal with the two photographs simultaneously and thus save some time. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall looking at these photographs, and based upon your knowledge, having been to the scene of the site, what walls or portions of the structure are depicted in these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That's the wall on the east side of the structure, and it's an area that's not even near the lower basement area. That's the area that we're talking about that's supported on the ground. The basement has nothing to affect or deal with that area. What we're seeing there are some bricks that are obviously collapsing more than likely due to the severe moisture that's within the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say we're seeing some bricks that are obviously collapsing, it would be helpful, I think, if you could use the drawing tool again with the assistance of the court staff to demarcate or identify the specific bricks that you are making reference to.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That'd be in these areas here and here. They're failing more than likely due to all the damage, the severe moisture, and again, the building of the lower basement area is nowhere near this. This is approximately 6 to 8 feet away that's sitting on top of the landscape or dirt itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can just back up a bit. It's been -- it's been postulated by the Prosecution, I believe using these -- the same photographs, that an air fuel explosion of some type took place within the basement room that was the subject of the investigation and caused the damage; that is to say the damage to these bricks that is evidenced on this side of the structure that you have now circled. What do you have to say as to that? Do you agree with that being a likelihood or even a probability?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It's not a probability due to the fact the basement structure is below level. This is above level, and the shockwave would have to again penetrate through -- we're talking 6 to 8 feet of dirt, whereas have you a wall directly in the basement that's still intact and did not fail.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so we can back up a bit, perhaps there was one item I ought to have gone through with you before, but you attended the Post-Blast Investigation School of the FBI in 2005, according to your curriculum vitae. Could you please detail for us, first of all, what -- to whom that course was offered by the US Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigations and what curricula you covered therein, what types of things you were specifically trained to look for.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I was put on by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and it was put out to our department, the fire investigators, and the local police department; and it basically taught us how to identify signs of blast, how to reconstruct a scene that has been involved in a blast, including the reconstruction of any type of device and specifically with IEDs or improvised explosive device, something that somebody would just make up in a time of war, and how to reconstruct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in conjunction with that, I see in 2002 you also attended a course, I believe, in conjunction with the Department of Justice and the National Emergency Response as to weapons of mass destruction, terrorism. Whereas did you have any training as to -- instruction as to blast, post-blast investigations arising therefrom?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Actually, I attended I believe it was three altogether, weapons of mass destruction, but they dealt on different aspects other than post-blast. They were more for biological, chemical warfare as well as the treatment of patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your employment with the fire department, have you -- and specifically your employment as an arson/fire investigator within that division, have you had occasion to deal with structural fires that you have investigated that were the result of so-called air fuel explosions?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I have. During my time in the department, I have personally been the lead on four structure fires that have been involved in a blast due to this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get back to your specific observations of the basement room, but since we're dealing with this now, I want to ask you: Based upon your knowledge and experience and what you saw at the scene with your own eyes, do you consider it to be likely that an air fuel explosion took place and caused the damage in the basement room of the Pionirska Street location?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No, it is not, but then again I wasn't directed to look for -- examination of that nature. I did review and make note of things I saw, and I saw nothing of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could save this and tender it as the next available 1D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D186, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can return to where we were going before, which was your external examination of the structure. If we could focus now once again on the room, the basement room. First of all, what can you tell us about the entranceway to that room? What stood out for you or struck your attention as you examined the entranceway to that basement room where it is alleged that this fire occurred and that many persons perished?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Well, initially walking up to the door we're looking at the roof area where the portico was, specifically in front of the doorway. Again, since it's a doorway, that's an opening for fire to travel out of. We initially saw what appeared as black staining, so basically examined it more thoroughly, and it was determined that it was mold of some type, and it varied in colours from green to dark black, and it's very moist and damp.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to hold you up there for a second just to explain to us. Now, you say you examine it more thoroughly, and it was determined that it was mold of some type. Could you describe for us what you physically did with the door frame to ascertain whether the darkened area was mold or fire damage or smoke damage.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Well, after noting the ceiling area outside the door, I also checked the door frame itself, and the dark areas followed the travel line of the water and moisture. So to see if that was mold or not, I actually scraped my finger across of it to see if it would come off like normal residue of ash, which it did not. It was slimy to the touch, and it was more like a mold. Anybody who's dealt with fires at all knows that ash is very dry and powder-like.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up, I believe, 1D165. I believe this is an exhibit that we used with Mr. McCoy. Rather than calling up a new one, I think we can make use of it if it's not too marked up. Actually, I guess it is mark up. If we could go to -- pull up Y020-3527, please, and that should hopefully give us the document on the right. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, looking at this photograph, is this the door frame that you were talking about, and could you please indicate for us using the pen what portion of the door frame you tested and the manner that you described with your finger to ascertain what the cause was of the darkened appearance of the material. I apologise. You should always wait for the court usher. I should have made that clear earlier.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Where I scraped it was just in this area right here because there's already scrape marks in the other areas, so I didn't want to compromise that, and this was done after Mr. McCoy had already photographed it, so you wouldn't see my scrape on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, what can you tell us -- you've already told us how you determined that it was mold. What can you tell us about the appearance of this discolouration? Would it -- the location of the darkening, did that also provide any kind of clues as to whether, in fact, it was due to fire or to some other cause?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: While examining that upper beam, it was noted that it followed the travel line of moisture. If you note it traveling this direction, it actually ties in with this water pattern, as well, and it also seeped into this beam here, so it had the appearance of actually going with the water, and that's how it got saturated and became moldy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I guess for the record, we should indicate that the red enclosed rectangular shape in the middle of the door frame was the initial marking by the witness, and all other markings in red are the subsequent markings that he has just made demonstrating the path of water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was the area there moist to the touch?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- we can't see in this photograph. Let me see if I can find another photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have this admitted as the next 1D exhibit number, and then I believe we can then move on to ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D187, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If we could go to P280.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was going to ask you about that piece of wood to the left of the door jamb, but I think the next exhibit is a depiction of it. Now, sir, do you recognise this portion of the door frame, and did you, in fact, ascertain any empirical findings and make any conclusions as to the darkened or discoloured portions of this wood material?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I noticed this as being similar to the door shim, which is basically just described -- it's a piece of wood to support this door jamb and keep it level and upright and straight, and in regards to this I did look at this for any type of burn patterns. I didn't find any. What I found was more mold.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you do the same type of physical testing?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I ran my fingers along it and just looked at it. Again, on any wood surface, I'm looking for any type of charring, alligatoring, I mean, even just soot. Didn't find any alligatoring. Everything's still smooth. As far as soot, again, it was still slimy to the touch, and if you look in this area right here - I'll draw next to it - you can actually see, it's actually more like it's seeping into the wood whereas burn actually would burn it, and if the flame is coming -- or fire is coming out of that hole, it would be lapping around the wool.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've made a marking in red ink noting where you said the mold was seeping into the wood. If I could ask you to perhaps choose a different-colour marker and indicate by way of lines and an arrow what direction you would expect a fire to be lapping over across the wood as you just actually indicated, if it were coming out of the door.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Actually, on this portion I was looking it, if it was coming out of the door frame, where this is fitted through; so I was looking at seeing if fire was coming out of here, because it's an obvious gap, and there was none, so we'd see lapping over this area, and we do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for purposes of memorializing the record, we would reflect that the blue arrows are the mark-up of this photograph that you have done to indicate that, and just to make clear, the light blue circle was already on the photograph, and have you not made that marking; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That is correct, and I would like to state one more thing. This is also on the interior of the structure. You can tell that by the door. It's opened in, and that's one thing we note, the door opens inward, so this is inside the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can have, then, this saved and admitted as the next 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D188, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I make a correction? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I was looking at this incorrectly. That is the exterior. The door I'm looking at in the background is actually opening inwards. I'm sorry. My perspective was incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- okay. And with respect to the exterior review of the structure, of the -- pardon me, the interior view of the basement room because, of course, we all agree that there was some sort of a fire on the upper floors of the structure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Focussing on the basement room, the door of which we were just looking at, could you tell us with respect to that whether, in fact, you found any signs on the exterior of the structure indicating the likelihood or probability that that fire was evidence, that a large or fully enveloped fire emanating from that basement room was evidence. Was there any signs of that on the exterior?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No, there was not. Normally in a multi-storey structure, we look at all the openings, again, the doors and windows because that's the best way for a fire to travel is upwards; and we found no indication of a fire coming out the door or two windows extending to the upward area that did show fire damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then one more from the exterior before we move to the interior. I'm just trying to find the appropriate picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I guess we'll just call it up as a new one: Y020-3541, I think is the one we're needing to look at. Hasn't been attached. Let me try and find -- well, let's move on, then. If we find it we'll get back to it, but I'd like to proceed further.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, after completing the visible physical inspection of the exterior of the room in question, what could you tell us when you move to the interior of the room what -- how did your investigation proceed, and what first jumped out at you or struck you as interesting and of help to you in reaching the conclusions that you reached in your report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Well, initially entering into the structure, again, we used a systematic approach. Normally in a larger structure we'd go around the full building. Since this was a singular room, I just made entry into it, and the first thing I noticed was the lack of flooring and approximately two-thirds of it. So in that regard, I started inspecting the dirt itself for any signs or remains of a fire or fire debris.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, could you explain for us, what is the process that you normally would employ based upon your knowledge and experience in which you did employ at the site in question to check for any signs of fire or fire debris as regards to the dirt, the exposed dirt on the floor?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: What I did in the area where the dirt was, again, it's two-thirds of that room, and the room, again, is 13 feet by 18 feet. And up until where the wood planks are, I -- in various locations, I actually dug into the dirt looking for some type of ash, wood chunks, burn chunks, any type of wood debris that would normally be left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you say that would normally be left behind. What is your experience and what has been your experience with regards to your occupation as to whether this debris can be completely cleaned out by -- cleaned up enough by an untrained person who is not a fire investigator so as to remove all trace material?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It's unlikely. There's no way to get down deep enough. Even if you had people walking on it, you'd find some sort of ash in relationship to it. It's nearly impossible, or it is impossible, actually, to remove everything out of a building, to save -- to clean it up, in your words, I believe it was. You find something in every fire, and that's what my job, is is to go in and find evidence in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if you could explain something for us, in your line of work when you're looking for such debris, for instance, in this case in a dirt area, are you looking for large pieces, small pieces? I mean, what type of matter are -- what size does the matter you're looking for typically come in?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Actually, I'm looking for any and all, big, small, down to ash. Again, any signs of fire, any type of evidence that might indicate a fire. You know, during a normal investigation, you don't discount anything you find. You must rule, look at everything, make a note of it, and then take the totality of your investigation to come to your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber apologises for the delay. We have had to be consulting on some of the issues raised in the case. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've used the time efficiently and I've located the missing photograph that we had prior of the doorway, just to finish that off before we return to the floor boards, Mr. Dimas. If I can have the assistance of the court usher or court officer to call up Y020-3543.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when that photograph comes up, sir, I will again ask you to review the same and advise us if you recall this particular feature of the door, and if you could describe for us what your trained eyes see with respect to the same. And if need be, if you need to use a pen, please wait for the court assistant to assist you.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: That's the other side of the door frame in the upper corner. Again, this is the area that we're talking about earlier. Approximately after the photos were taken, this area here is where I actually scraped from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record -- let the report reflect that you have marked in red ink a circle towards the right-hand side of the photograph. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: It was determined that everything in the area here was mold as well as over here. Again, this also shows the travel of the water coming down in the same direction that I point out earlier. Again, on this edge of the beam, what I was looking at is this area right here. That's where the water has been soaking into the wood, which follows that line, and the mold has been going into the wood. In relation to this superior portion --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could -- for purposes of preserving the record, let the record reflect that the left-most red line on the portion of the wood wedge or shim, I think you had called it previously, is what's been referred to by the witness. Now, sir, if you're going to mark any further, I would ask with the assistance of the court staff that you change colours so that we don't lose track of what is being depicted by you in these photographs.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: What I also did was these areas here or the gaps between the wood, I was looking inside that area that area there; again I'm looking for fire patterns, soot, debris, any type of indication that fire was rolling through that area. It also aided me, or what I was looking for was to see if this door frame was there at the time of the fire or after the fire. Either way, there should have been some type of damage in between there if this door was here now or afterwards. You would find something between where this jamb was because of the size of the gap.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, from this photograph we see sort of the rough appearance of the -- I guess it's concrete that's up by the door. In your experience, given the rough nature of the surface that is involved by the door frame and by the door jamb, would it be possible -- strike that. Would it be probable that someone could -- again, an untrained person could clean all trace matter and are all evidence from that location?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: No. There's just too many little cracks or gaps within all this mortar and concrete to just scrub everything out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is there anything else you need to tell us with respect to this photograph, or shall I tender it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: You can tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the photograph as marked be tendered as the next available 1D exhibit number with the caveat that the blue markings are the most recent markings on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D189, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, before the break we were talking about the area of the floor inside the basement, and you had indicated that you had performed some tests to poke into the dirt to see if you could find any evidence of debris that you would have expected resulting from a fire. You indicated that two-thirds, approximately, of the interior floor was exposed dirt. Could you tell us, did you check in one area, multiple areas, and if so, how many areas approximately did you check in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: I approximately did five areas around that two-third area. Basically, I did almost like a square pattern. I did corners of that open area and then one in the centre. I felt that would give me the best probability of finding something in the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now I'm going to give you somewhat of a hypothetical. In your opinion based upon your experience and your knowledge, if there had been a fire and either the wood in that two-thirds-exposed area had been completely consumed or burnt up or had been removed after the fact by someone using tools, would you still expect to have found something?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I would. You just can't get rid of everything. If you start at one spot, you might stop on another spot, put a [indiscernible] in the ground. There's just no way to get rid of everything. You might get rid of the larger debris and scoop it up, but to remove ash totally, you can't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me turn to Y020-3618, and alongside that if we could have Y020-3617.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, now I'd like to start examining the wood interior. First of all -- I will wait for the picture to resize. I guess -- if that can --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Maybe I'm just causing too much confusion this way. If we can just pull up one of the photographs, perhaps the 3618 by itself. Maybe that'll just be easier than trying to orientate them lengthwise. And I believe that needs to be flipped -- rotated, pardon me, 90 degrees. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, was there a portion of the interior floor that was still intact, that is to say where the wood floor beams were still intact?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. That was approximately the one-third area that I was talking about versus the two-thirds of dirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if I can direct your attention to the dark areas in the -- correct me if I'm wrong. This is a corner of the room that is depicted in this photograph; is that accurate?
